384	Goal: implement the M7 follow-ups #1 and #4 together — `kca skill run`
385	without `--dry-run` now drives an `AgentWorker` whose tool calls are
386	gated by the M7 permission policy and respect the ToolSpec metadata.
387	
388	Step 1 — `kca skill run <name> [--mode <mode>] --execute` (or drop --dry-run
389	to keep the existing flag shape):
390	  - Build a JobPolicy:
391	      policy = JobPolicy(
392	          skill_name=name,
393	          allowed_tools=skill.meta.allowed_tools,
394	          approval_gates={
395	              tool: resolve_for_skill(skill.meta, tool, mode=args.mode)
396	              for tool in skill.meta.allowed_tools
397	          },
398	          max_turns=..., max_cost_usd=..., max_runtime_s=...,
399	      )
400	  - Create the agent_job row via tools/kca/db.create_agent_job(skill_name=name,
401	    policy=policy, rendered_prompt=rendered_body, …).
402	  - Hand to AgentWorker.run(job_id).
403	
404	Step 2 — In src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call:
405	  - Resolve the ToolSpec via tool_registry.get_tool(tool_name).
406	  - Enforce ToolSpec.timeout_s as a hard timeout (use signal/alarm or
407	    subprocess.run timeout depending on the tool implementation).
408	  - Honour ToolSpec.sandbox:
409	      "sandboxed"          → run in current process (no extra escape).
410	      "unsandboxed"        → require approval_label resolved to "allow"
411	                             OR a satisfied approval gate from policy.
412	      "isolated_workspace" → cwd must be the job's workspace path.
413	  - Cross-check JobPolicy.approval_gates[tool_name]:
414	      "allow" → proceed.
415	      "ask"   → write human_decisions row + agent_job_events("decision_pending")
416	                + return a paused-job marker; do NOT execute.
417	      "deny"  → raise PolicyViolation, mark job failed.
418	  - On any decision, call audit.log_policy_decision(...) so the
419	    `agent_tool_audit` table records the outcome.

726	
727	```
728	Read:
729	1. supabase/migrations/0003_m3_worker.sql       (human_decisions)
730	2. supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql (agent_reviews)

732	4. tools/kca/decisions.py                       (approve / reject CLI)
733	5. tools/kca/agent/permission_policy.py         (decision semantics)
734	6. docs/milestones.md   (M8 § Decision-gate UI requirements)
735	
736	Goal: the most important M8 page. A human sees every pending decision,
737	approves / rejects / asks-the-agent-to-improve, and the write path goes
738	through the EXISTING `kca decisions` mechanism — the browser never
739	bypasses the permission policy.
740	
741	Step 1 — `ui/src/pages/ApprovalInbox.tsx`:
742	  - List human_decisions where status = 'pending'.
743	  - Columns: operation, run_id link, requested_at, policy_profile,
744	    reviewer_verdict (from agent_reviews if any), action link.
745	  - Default sort: oldest first ("FIFO so nothing rots").
746	
747	Step 2 — `ui/src/pages/DecisionGate.tsx` (route /approvals/:id):
748	  Show the full context required by the milestone spec:
749	    - operation
750	    - cv_score (joined from runs.metric_value where metric_name='cv_score')
751	    - cost_so_far (joined from agent_jobs.cost_so_far)
752	    - artifact preview (top 50 lines if the file is text and < 1 MB;
753	      otherwise a download link only — never preview binaries inline)
754	    - reviewer verdict + reasoning (from agent_reviews)
755	    - recent tool audit entries for the job (from agent_tool_audit)
756	
757	  Three actions:
758	    - Approve  → POST to action service (Step 3) with reason field optional.
759	    - Reject   → POST with reason required (UI enforces minLength=8).
760	    - Ask agent to improve → POST with a structured "feedback" payload
761	      (free text + optional metric_target). The backend appends to
762	      `agent_job_events` and resumes the job at the next planning turn.
763	
764	  All three actions disable buttons immediately and show a spinner until
765	  the response comes back. On success, redirect to /approvals.
766	
767	Step 3 — Action service:
768	  Stand up a tiny FastAPI app at `services/decision_api/` (Python).
769	    POST /decision/:id/approve
770	    POST /decision/:id/reject
771	    POST /decision/:id/ask-improve
772	  Each endpoint:
773	    - Validates the user (M8 ships local-only: simple HMAC over
774	      `KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN`; UI reads token from a same-origin
775	      cookie set out-of-band by `kca ui login`).
776	    - Calls the existing functions in tools/kca/decisions.py.
777	    - Writes audit via tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision.
778	  Wire pnpm dev's vite.config.ts to proxy `/api/*` to localhost:8787.
779	
780	UI rules:
781	  - The browser cannot construct a `kaggle competitions submit` call; it
782	    can only call /decision/:id/approve. The actual submit still flows
783	    through the worker after the approval is recorded.
784	  - "Approve" button is RED-DESTRUCTIVE-style if the operation is
785	    SUBMISSION-class (kaggle_submit, kernel_push, supabase_migrate),
786	    AMBER-CAUTION-style otherwise.
787	  - Decision changes are atomic: the API rejects with 409 if the
788	    decision is already non-pending.
789

998	## Overview
999	One paragraph: M8 surfaces the M2–M7 control plane as a read-mostly UI.
1000	The browser never writes to Supabase directly except through the
1001	decision_api action service, which routes through the existing
1002	`tools/kca/decisions.py` paths so M7 policy gates stay authoritative.
1003	
1004	## Layer map
1005	Diagram (ASCII) of:
1006	  Browser (Vite SPA) → Supabase JS (read) → Postgres
1007	                    → /api/decision/* → decision_api → kca decisions → Postgres
1008	                                                                       → worker resume
1009	
1010	## Data flow per page
1011	For each of: Dashboard, RunTimeline, Experiments, Research, ApprovalInbox,
1012	DecisionGate, Artifacts — list the tables read and the joins performed.
1013	
1014	## Auth model
1015	- Local-only token via KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN.
1016	- M8 ships single-user; multi-user lands in M9 or later.
1017	- No service-role key ever reaches the browser.
1018	
1019	## Approval gate semantics
1020	- "Approve" / "Reject" / "Ask agent to improve" map to existing
1021	  `tools/kca/decisions.py` functions.
1022	- The browser cannot mutate `agent_jobs.status` directly; only the
1023	  action service can, and only via the kca decisions API.
1024	- M7 permission_policy.resolve_for_skill is the source of truth for
1025	  which operations need a decision; UI is purely a presentation layer.
1026	
1027	## Audit trail
1028	- Every action service mutation writes a row to `agent_tool_audit`.
1029	- `.agent/audit.jsonl` continues to exist for offline ops; the dual-write
1030	  behaviour from M8-T001 keeps both backends in sync when DB is available.
1031	
1032	## Adding a new page
1033	Step-by-step: add route → add typed query in `ui/src/lib/db.ts` →
1034	add page component → write vitest test → optional Playwright case.
1035	
1036	## Adding a new approve-class operation
1037	Step-by-step: add ToolSpec to TOOL_REGISTRY (M7) → add policy record →
1038	add decision_api wiring → render in DecisionGate.

# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-21 (M7 exit)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, and approvals.
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

## Completed milestones
- **M0**: project baseline and memory discipline ✓
- **M1**: local Kaggle tooling wrapper baseline ✓
- **M2**: Supabase/control plane foundation ✓
- **M3**: Python-first competition worker v0 ✓
- **M4**: Kaggle competition workflow v0 ✓
- **M5**: research and browser workflow ✓
- **M6**: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓
- **M7**: KCA CLI architecture (command / skill / tool / permission policy) ✓

See `docs/m7-final-review.md` for M7 validation results (28/28 checks PASS).

## Current milestone: M8 — product UI shell

Status: planned. Expose the control plane through a React/TypeScript UI (Next.js or Vite) built in Claude Code: approval inbox, run timeline, experiment table, artifact browser. M7 follow-ups (skill → worker wiring, DB audit table, tool executor integration) tracked in `docs/m7-final-review.md` § M8 follow-ups.

## Open decisions
- TypeScript-only platform service vs TypeScript API + Python worker from day one (M8 concern).
- Supabase queue/job mechanism for first use (SQS-style or Supabase Queues).
- First cloud deployment target: AWS vs GCP (M8+ concern; local-first until then).
- Model routing policy thresholds: Sonnet for implement, Opus for eval/analysis, Haiku/local for triage.

> Give the KCA platform a stable, inspectable CLI architecture with four
> explicit layers: **Command**, **Skill**, **Tool**, **Job**. Ship a skill
> loader, a tool registry, a permission policy layer with `allow | ask | deny`
> resolution, the `kca skill list / show / run` and `kca tool list / audit /
> doctor` subcommands, four seed skills, audit logging to `.agent/audit.jsonl`,

`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres` connects directly to
the `supabase-db` container; the host-port-mapped `localhost:5432` is the

file-first, so the live-db check is informational only — M7 itself adds no
new migrations.

## What landed

### New code

- `tools/kca/agent/__init__.py` — package marker.
- `tools/kca/agent/skill_loader.py` — `SkillMeta`, `Skill`, `load_skill`,
  `list_skills`, `render_skill`; YAML frontmatter parser; `$arg` substitution.
- `tools/kca/agent/command_registry.py` — `CommandSpec`, `CommandRegistry`,
  module-level `REGISTRY` seeded with 12 commands (10 existing + `skill` +
  `tool`).
- `tools/kca/agent/tool_registry.py` — `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_REGISTRY` (16 tools),
  `get_tool`, `list_tools`, `default_decision`. Constants for valid
  side-effect / approval / sandbox labels.
- `tools/kca/agent/permission_policy.py` — `PolicyRecord`, `PermissionPolicy`,
  `load_policy`, `resolve_for_skill`. Resolution priority:
  deny > mode-allow > default_decision > tool default > "ask".
- `tools/kca/agent/audit.py` — `AuditRecord`, `AuditLogger` (file + optional
  DB), `log_policy_decision`. `args_hash` (SHA-256), not raw args.

- `tools/kca/tool.py` — `kca tool list / audit / doctor`.

  `REGISTRY.list_all()` so new commands auto-register.

- `.kca/permissions/default.yaml` — conservative profile; submissions ask.
- `.kca/permissions/permissive-dev.yaml` — bash + git allowed; submissions ask.
- `.kca/permissions/competition-runner.yaml` — kaggle_submit allowed only in
  `competition-finalization` / `human-approved` modes; `budget_exceeded: deny`.

### Tests + docs

- `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` — 214-line architecture doc.

## M8 follow-ups

1. **Wire skill execution through the worker.** M7 ships the CLI surface
   only; `kca skill run <name>` (no `--dry-run`) emits audit + a note. M8
   should pipe a rendered skill body into `AgentWorker` with the resolved
   `JobPolicy.approval_gates` populated from `resolve_for_skill`.
2. **DB-side audit table.** `audit.py` currently best-efforts into
   `agent_job_events` with `event_type="tool_audit"`; add a dedicated
   `agent_tool_audit` migration + view if the volume justifies it.
3. **Skill schema validation.** Add a JSON-Schema gate for SKILL.md
   frontmatter so malformed seed skills fail at `list_skills()` instead of
   silently skipping.
4. **Tool registry → worker tool executor.** Hook `ToolSpec.timeout_s`,
   `sandbox`, and `approval_label` into `src/worker/worker.py::_tool_call` so
   the runtime path matches the declared policy.
5. **`.kca/skills/_test_fixture/`.** Either delete after the smoke tests
   stop depending on a real-skill fixture, or rename to a real platform
   skill.
6. **CI live-db job.** `live-db` job exists in the workflow file but has not
   been exercised on PRs yet; confirm secret wiring and gate fork forks.

"""Audit logger: records policy decisions for tool executions to JSONL/DB."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import uuid
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _repo_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _default_audit_path() -> Path:
    return _repo_root() / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"


@dataclass
class AuditRecord:
    timestamp: str
    session_id: str
    skill_name: str | None
    tool_name: str
    operation: str
    decision: str
    mode: str
    policy_profile: str
    audit_required: bool
    args_hash: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


def _hash_args(args: dict | None) -> str:
    if not args:
        return ""
    try:
        serialized = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    except TypeError:
        serialized = str(sorted(args.items()))
    return hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


_SESSION_ID = os.environ.get("KCA_SESSION_ID") or str(uuid.uuid4())


@dataclass
class AuditLogger:
    backend: str = "file"  # "file" | "db" | "both"
    file_path: Path = field(default_factory=_default_audit_path)
    db_available: bool = False
    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: _SESSION_ID)

    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] mkdir failed: {exc}\n")

    def record(self, rec: AuditRecord) -> None:
        if self.backend in ("file", "both"):
            self._ensure_dir()
            try:
                with self.file_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    fh.write(json.dumps(rec.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            except OSError as exc:
                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] write failed: {exc}\n")

        if self.backend in ("db", "both") and self.db_available:
            try:
                from db import append_job_event  # type: ignore

                append_job_event(
                    job_id=str(uuid.UUID(int=0)),
                    event_type="tool_audit",
                    event_data=rec.to_dict(),
                )
            except Exception as exc:
                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] db append failed: {exc}\n")

    def log_policy_decision(
        self,
        *,
        tool: str,
        operation: str,
        decision: str,
        skill_name: str | None = None,
        mode: str = "default",
        policy_profile: str = "default",
        args: dict | None = None,
        audit_required: bool = False,
    ) -> AuditRecord:
        rec = AuditRecord(
            timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
```

```markdown
# ADR-0014: UI Stack — Vite + React + TypeScript

## Status

Accepted (M8).

## Context

M8 ships the first human-facing surface on top of the M2–M7 control plane. The
target user is an operator/dev who runs Kaggle/CTF experiments locally and
needs to approve gated operations, inspect runs, browse research and
artifacts, and watch the audit trail.

Two viable shapes were considered:

- **A) Next.js (app router)** — file-based routing, React Server Components,
  API routes baked in.
- **B) Vite + React + React Router** — pure SPA, no SSR, no API routes.

## Decision

**B — Vite + React + React Router.**

Rationale:

- The product is an operator/dev workbench, not a public site. SEO and SSR are
  non-goals; first paint over a few KB of HTML is good enough.
- Backend writes already live in `tools/kca/*` and `src/worker/`. The UI does
  not need API routes — it talks to Supabase for reads and to a small
  Python/FastAPI action service (`services/decision_api/`, M8-T009) for
  writes. That service is the only path that can mutate `human_decisions`
  rows, and it re-uses the existing `tools/kca/decisions.py` so the M7
  `permission_policy` resolution stays authoritative.
- Vite's dev loop (HMR, no compile-stage gymnastics) matches the Claude Code
  editing cadence better than Next's RSC/route-tree dance.
- Smaller dependency surface to keep safe with the M7 permission policy: we
  do not introduce a server runtime we have to harden against SSR-side data
  leaks.

## Consequences

- All authenticated mutations go through `services/decision_api/` (or future
  Supabase RPC functions). The browser bundle **never** holds a
  service-role key; it uses the anon key + RLS, and writes via the action
  service over `/api/*`.
- Server-rendered features (social previews, SEO landing pages) are
  explicitly out of scope for M8. If we need them later, we can either move
  to Next.js or front the SPA with a tiny edge renderer.
- `pnpm` is the package manager (Vite scaffolds support it cleanly and the CI
  job in M8-T011 standardises on it).
- TypeScript is strict (`tsc --noEmit --strict` is part of CI).
- Tailwind CSS provides styling primitives without a design-system dep; raw
  Tailwind + Headless UI is sufficient for the M8 page set.
- Test stack: Vitest + React Testing Library for unit, Playwright for e2e.

## Alternatives considered

- **Next.js app router** — rejected per the rationale above. We may revisit
  if M9+ needs SSR/edge.
- **Remix** — similar trade-offs to Next; the SSR benefits do not apply to
  an internal operator UI.
- **Svelte / SolidJS** — smaller community, less Claude Code editing inertia
  in this codebase, and the team has more React experience.

```
</details>

### ✍️  Write `0014-ui-stack.md`

<details>
<summary><code>/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/.claude/worktrees/m8-loop/docs/adr/0014-ui-stack.md</code></summary>

```markdown
# ADR-0014: UI Stack — Vite + React + TypeScript

## Status

Accepted (M8).

## Context

M8 ships the first human-facing surface on top of the M2–M7 control plane. The
target user is an operator/dev who runs Kaggle/CTF experiments locally and
needs to approve gated operations, inspect runs, browse research and
artifacts, and watch the audit trail.

Two viable shapes were considered:

- **A) Next.js (app router)** — file-based routing, React Server Components,
  API routes baked in.
- **B) Vite + React + React Router** — pure SPA, no SSR, no API routes.

> Note on numbering: the M8 loop prompt named this ADR "0011" but
> `0011-local-model-endpoints.md` already exists. The next free slot is
> `0014`, which is what we use here.

## Decision

**B — Vite + React + React Router.**

Rationale:

- The product is an operator/dev workbench, not a public site. SEO and SSR are
  non-goals; first paint over a few KB of HTML is good enough.
- Backend writes already live in `tools/kca/*` and `src/worker/`. The UI does
  not need API routes — it talks to Supabase for reads and to a small
  Python/FastAPI action service (`services/decision_api/`, M8-T009) for
  writes. That service is the only path that can mutate `human_decisions`
  rows, and it re-uses the existing `tools/kca/decisions.py` so the M7
  `permission_policy` resolution stays authoritative.
- Vite's dev loop (HMR, no compile-stage gymnastics) matches the Claude Code
  editing cadence better than Next's RSC/route-tree dance.
- Smaller dependency surface to keep safe with the M7 permission policy: we
  do not introduce a server runtime we have to harden against SSR-side data
  leaks.

## Consequences

- All authenticated mutations go through `services/decision_api/` (or future
  Supabase RPC functions). The browser bundle **never** holds a
  service-role key; it uses the anon key + RLS, and writes via the action
  service over `/api/*`.
- Server-rendered features (social previews, SEO landing pages) are
  explicitly out of scope for M8. If we need them later, we can either move
  to Next.js or front the SPA with a tiny edge renderer.
- `pnpm` is the package manager (Vite scaffolds support it cleanly and the CI
  job in M8-T011 standardises on it).
- TypeScript is strict (`tsc --noEmit --strict` is part of CI).
- Tailwind CSS provides styling primitives without a design-system dep; raw
  Tailwind + Headless UI is sufficient for the M8 page set.
- Test stack: Vitest + React Testing Library for unit, Playwright for e2e.

## Alternatives considered

- **Next.js app router** — rejected per the rationale above. We may revisit
  if M9+ needs SSR/edge.
- **Remix** — similar trade-offs to Next; the SSR benefits do not apply to
  an internal operator UI.
- **Svelte / SolidJS** — smaller community, less Claude Code editing inertia
  in this codebase, and the team has more React experience.

```
</details>

322	) -> dict:

325	            """
326	            insert into experiment_run_metrics
327	              (experiment_run_id, key, value, metadata)
328	            values (%s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
329	            returning id, key, value, recorded_at

342	                              jsonb_build_object('value', %s::numeric, 'recorded_at', now())
343	                            )
344	              where id = %s::uuid
345	            """,

362	def _list_runs_m2(
363	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
364	    competition_slug: str | None,
365	    limit: int,
366	) -> list[dict]:
367	    # Note: competitions is not directly linked to experiments yet; for M2 we
368	    # filter via run_dir prefix (runs/<slug>/...) until a join column is added.
369	    query = """
370	        select
371	          er.id::text          as experiment_run_id,
372	          er.external_run_id   as run_id,
373	          er.run_dir,
374	          er.metrics,
375	          er.created_at,
376	          e.id::text           as experiment_id,
377	          e.name               as experiment_name,
378	          e.hypothesis,
379	          e.tags
380	        from experiment_runs er
381	        join experiments e on e.id = er.experiment_id
382	        {where}
383	        order by er.created_at desc
384	        limit %s
385	    """
386	    params: list[Any] = []
387	    if competition_slug:
388	        query = query.format(where="where er.run_dir like %s")
389	        params.append(f"runs/{competition_slug}/%")
390	    else:
391	        query = query.format(where="")
392	    params.append(limit)
393	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
394	        cur.execute(query, params)
395	        rows = cur.fetchall()

415	              e.id::text          as experiment_id
416	            from experiment_runs er
417	            join experiments e on e.id = er.experiment_id
418	            where er.run_dir = %s
419	            order by er.created_at desc
420	            limit 1
421	            """,
422	            (run_dir,),
423	        )
424	        row = cur.fetchone()
425	    return dict(row) if row else None

555	def _create_job(
556	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
557	    project_id: str,
558	    prompt: str,
559	    policy: dict,
560	    model: str,
561	    competition_slug: str | None,

578	              (project_id, session_id, competition_id, status, payload,
579	               prompt, model, policy)
580	            VALUES
581	              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, 'queued', %s::jsonb,
582	               %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
583	            RETURNING id::text
584	            """,
585	            (
586	                project_id,
587	                session_id,
588	                competition_id,
589	                json.dumps(policy),
590	                prompt,
591	                model,
592	                json.dumps(policy),
593	            ),
594	        )
595	        row = cur.fetchone()
596	    conn.commit()
597	    assert row is not None
598	    return row["id"]

618	def lease_job(
619	    job_id: str,
620	    worker_id: str,
621	    lease_seconds: int = 300,
622	    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
623	) -> bool:
624	    """Atomically set status='running', leased_by, leased_until.
625	
626	    Returns True if successfully leased, False if already running/leased.
627	    """
628	    return _with_conn(conn, _lease_job, job_id, worker_id, lease_seconds)

630	
631	def _lease_job(
632	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
633	    job_id: str,
634	    worker_id: str,
635	    lease_seconds: int,
636	) -> bool:
637	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
638	        cur.execute(
639	            """
640	            UPDATE agent_jobs
641	               SET status = 'running',
642	                   leased_by = %s,
643	                   leased_until = now() + (%s || ' seconds')::interval,
644	                   started_at = COALESCE(started_at, now())
645	             WHERE id = %s::uuid
646	               AND status IN ('queued', 'paused')
647	            """,
648	            (worker_id, str(lease_seconds), job_id),
649	        )
650	        updated = cur.rowcount
651	    conn.commit()
652	    return updated > 0

967	def _create_experiment_m4(
968	    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
969	    competition_id: str,
970	    hypothesis: str,
971	    job_id: str | None,
972	    branch: str | None,
973	    config: dict,
974	) -> str:
975	    # The M1 experiments table requires project_id + name; the M4 INSERT must
976	    # populate them as well so both schema shapes coexist on the same row.
977	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
978	        cur.execute(
979	            "SELECT project_id::text FROM competitions WHERE id = %s::uuid",
980	            (competition_id,),
981	        )
982	        comp_row = cur.fetchone()
983	        project_id = (comp_row or {}).get("project_id") or DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID
984	        synth_name = (branch or hypothesis or "m4-experiment")[:120]
985	        cur.execute(
986	            """
987	            INSERT INTO experiments
988	              (project_id, name, competition_id, job_id, hypothesis, branch, config)
989	            VALUES
990	              (%s::uuid, %s, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
991	            RETURNING id::text
992	            """,
993	            (
994	                project_id,
995	                synth_name,
996	                competition_id,
997	                job_id,
998	                hypothesis,
999	                branch,
1000	                json.dumps(config),
1001	            ),
1002	        )
1003	        row = cur.fetchone()
1004	    conn.commit()
1005	    assert row is not None
1006	    return row["id"]

1945	def _with_conn(conn, fn, *args, **kwargs):
1946	    """Call fn(conn, *args) using the provided conn or a freshly opened one.
1947	
1948	    When this function opens the connection, it also closes it.
1949	    """

-- 0007_m8_tool_audit.sql
-- M8: agent_tool_audit table + recent-audit view.
--
-- Forward-only. Idempotent. Additive. All indexes use IF NOT EXISTS so the
-- migration is safe to re-apply.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_tool_audit (
  id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  ts              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  session_id      UUID        NOT NULL,
  job_id          UUID        NULL REFERENCES agent_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  skill_name      TEXT        NULL,
  tool_name       TEXT        NOT NULL,
  operation       TEXT        NOT NULL,
  decision        TEXT        NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('allow', 'ask', 'deny')),
  mode            TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
  policy_profile  TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
  audit_required  BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  args_hash       TEXT        NOT NULL,
  extra           JSONB       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS agent_tool_audit_session_idx
  ON agent_tool_audit(session_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS agent_tool_audit_job_idx
  ON agent_tool_audit(job_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS agent_tool_audit_ts_idx
  ON agent_tool_audit(ts DESC);

ALTER TABLE agent_tool_audit ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_agent_tool_audit_recent AS
  SELECT
    a.*,
    j.policy AS job_policy,
    j.status AS job_status
  FROM agent_tool_audit a
  LEFT JOIN agent_jobs j ON j.id = a.job_id
  ORDER BY a.ts DESC
  LIMIT 200;

```python
"""Audit logger: records policy decisions for tool executions to JSONL/DB.

M7 shipped the JSONL backend at ``.agent/audit.jsonl``. M8 adds an optional
dual-write into the ``agent_tool_audit`` table (migration 0007) when
``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is set. The writer never raises on DB failure — the
JSONL line is always the source of truth for offline ops.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import uuid
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _repo_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _default_audit_path() -> Path:
    return _repo_root() / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"


@dataclass
class AuditRecord:
    timestamp: str
    session_id: str
    skill_name: str | None
    tool_name: str
    operation: str
    decision: str
    mode: str
    policy_profile: str
    audit_required: bool
    args_hash: str
    job_id: str | None = None
    extra: dict | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


def _hash_args(args: dict | None) -> str:
    if not args:
        return ""
    try:
        serialized = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    except TypeError:
        serialized = str(sorted(args.items()))
    return hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


_SESSION_ID = os.environ.get("KCA_SESSION_ID") or str(uuid.uuid4())


def _db_configured() -> bool:
    return bool(os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL") or os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_HOST"))


@dataclass
class AuditLogger:
    backend: str = "file"  # "file" | "db" | "both"
    file_path: Path = field(default_factory=_default_audit_path)
    db_available: bool | None = None
    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: _SESSION_ID)

    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] mkdir failed: {exc}\n")

    def _db_enabled(self) -> bool:
        if self.db_available is not None:
            return bool(self.db_available)
        return _db_configured()

    def record(self, rec: AuditRecord) -> None:
        if self.backend in ("file", "both"):
            self._ensure_dir()
            try:
                with self.file_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    fh.write(json.dumps(rec.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            except OSError as exc:
                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] write failed: {exc}\n")

        if self.backend in ("db", "both") and self._db_enabled():
            try:
                # Lazy import: keep the JSONL-only path free of psycopg.
                from tools.kca.db import insert_tool_audit  # type: ignore
            except Exception:
                try:
                    from db import insert_tool_audit  # type: ignore
                except Exception as exc:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] db module unavailable: {exc}\n")
                    return
            try:
                insert_tool_audit(rec.to_dict())
            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - best-effort DB
                sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] db insert failed: {exc}\n")

    def log_policy_decision(
        self,
        *,
        tool: str,
        operation: str,
        decision: str,
        skill_name: str | None = None,
        mode: str = "default",
        policy_profile: str = "default",
        args: dict | None = None,
        audit_required: bool = False,
        job_id: str | None = None,
        extra: dict | None = None,
    ) -> AuditRecord:
        rec = AuditRecord(
            timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            session_id=self.session_id,
            skill_name=skill_name,
            tool_name=tool,
            operation=operation,
            decision=decision,
            mode=mode,
            policy_profile=policy_profile,
            audit_required=audit_required,
            args_hash=_hash_args(args),
            job_id=job_id,
            extra=extra,
        )
        self.record(rec)
        return rec


def log_policy_decision(
    *,
    tool: str,
    operation: str,
    decision: str,
    skill_name: str | None = None,
    mode: str = "default",
    policy_profile: str = "default",
    args: dict | None = None,
    audit_required: bool = False,
    job_id: str | None = None,
    extra: dict | None = None,
    backend: str | None = None,
) -> AuditRecord:
    """Module-level shortcut that auto-selects backend based on env."""
    if backend is None:
        backend = "both" if _db_configured() else "file"
    logger = AuditLogger(backend=backend)
    return logger.log_policy_decision(
        tool=tool,
        operation=operation,
        decision=decision,
        skill_name=skill_name,
        mode=mode,
        policy_profile=policy_profile,
        args=args,
        audit_required=audit_required,
        job_id=job_id,
        extra=extra,
    )

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Backfill .agent/audit.jsonl into agent_tool_audit.

Idempotent: de-duplicates by (session_id, timestamp, tool_name).
Reads from the JSONL file, inserts each line into the M8 audit table.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Make tools/kca importable when running from the repo root.
REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(REPO) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
if str(REPO / "tools" / "kca") not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "tools" / "kca"))

from tools.kca.db import get_conn  # noqa: E402


def existing_keys(conn) -> set[tuple]:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT session_id::text, ts, tool_name FROM agent_tool_audit")
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return {(r["session_id"], r["ts"].isoformat(), r["tool_name"]) for r in rows}


def backfill(jsonl: Path, dry_run: bool = False) -> tuple[int, int]:
    if not jsonl.exists():
        print(f"no audit log at {jsonl}")
        return 0, 0
    conn = get_conn()
    try:
        seen = existing_keys(conn)
        inserted = 0
        skipped = 0
        with jsonl.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    rec = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                key = (rec.get("session_id"), rec.get("timestamp"), rec.get("tool_name"))
                if key in seen:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                if dry_run:
                    inserted += 1
                    continue
                with conn.cursor() as cur:
                    cur.execute(
                        """
                        INSERT INTO agent_tool_audit
                          (ts, session_id, job_id, skill_name, tool_name,
                           operation, decision, mode, policy_profile,
                           audit_required, args_hash, extra)
                        VALUES
                          (%s, %s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
                        """,
                        (
                            rec.get("timestamp"),
                            rec.get("session_id"),
                            rec.get("job_id"),
                            rec.get("skill_name"),
                            rec.get("tool_name"),
                            rec.get("operation"),
                            rec.get("decision"),
                            rec.get("mode", "default"),
                            rec.get("policy_profile", "default"),
                            bool(rec.get("audit_required", False)),
                            rec.get("args_hash", ""),
                            json.dumps(rec.get("extra") or {}),
                        ),
                    )
                    inserted += 1
        conn.commit()
        return inserted, skipped
    finally:
        conn.close()


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--jsonl", default=".agent/audit.jsonl", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args()
    inserted, skipped = backfill(args.jsonl, dry_run=args.dry_run)
    print(f"inserted={inserted} skipped={skipped} dry_run={args.dry_run}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```
</details>

1	# KCA CLI Architecture
2	
3	Status: M7 (2026-05-21).
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	KCA (Kaggle / CTF Code Agent) exposes two operator interfaces over the same
8	core. The **CLI** (`kca …`) is the deterministic, scriptable surface humans
9	and CI use directly. **Skills** are the agent-facing surface: declarative
10	Markdown recipes with YAML frontmatter that the agent worker can render and
11	execute. Both layers share the same tool registry and permission policy, so a
12	human running `kca kaggle submit` and an agent executing the `prepare-submission`
13	skill go through identical approval gates and audit records. M7 ships the
14	inspectable scaffold for both; M8 wires skill execution through the worker.
15	
16	## Four layers
17	
18	| Layer | Implemented in | Invocation | Side-effect control |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| Command | `tools/kca/*.py` | `kca <group> <cmd>` | `CommandSpec.side_effect` |
21	| Skill | `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | `kca skill run <name>` | `approval-policy` profile |
22	| Tool | `tools/kca/agent/tool_registry.py` | called by agent worker | `ToolSpec.approval_label` |
23	| Job | `src/worker/` + Supabase | `kca job run` (M8 wiring) | `JobPolicy` + budget tracker |
24	
25	Each layer has narrow responsibilities. The Command layer never reaches inside
26	the agent loop; the Skill layer never executes shell directly — it always
27	goes through tools — and the Tool layer is the only place where real side
28	effects (filesystem writes, network, Kaggle submission) actually occur.
29	
30	## Skill format
31	
32	Skills live at `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The file is parsed as YAML
33	frontmatter followed by a Markdown body.
34	
35	| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
36	|---|---|---|---|
37	| `name` | string | (required) | Slug used by `load_skill(name)`. Must match dir name. |
38	| `description` | string | (required) | One-line summary shown in `kca skill list`. |
39	| `version` | string | `"1.0"` | Free-form. |
40	| `argument-hint` | string | `""` | Human hint shown in CLI help. |
41	| `arguments` | list[string] | `[]` | Names of `$arg` tokens substituted into the body. |
42	| `allowed-tools` | list[string] | `[]` | Tool names from the tool registry. |
43	| `approval-policy` | string | `"default"` | Profile name in `.kca/permissions/`. |
44	| `disable-model-invocation` | bool | `false` | Reserved: prevent agent auto-invocation. |
45	| `tags` | list[string] | `[]` | Free-form labels for filtering. |
46	
47	Body tokens of the form `$name` are substituted at render time. Undeclared
48	tokens are passed through verbatim. Declared arguments not provided at render
49	time raise `ValueError`.
50	
```

127	## Audit trail
128	
129	Every non-dry-run skill invocation records a JSONL line to `.agent/audit.jsonl`
130	via `tools/kca/agent/audit.py`. An `AuditRecord` contains:
131	
132	- `timestamp` (ISO 8601 UTC)
133	- `session_id` (UUID stable per process)
134	- `skill_name`
135	- `tool_name` / `operation`
136	- `decision` (`allow` / `ask` / `deny`)
137	- `mode` and `policy_profile`
138	- `audit_required` flag (mirrors the policy record)
139	- `args_hash` — SHA-256 of serialised args, **not the args themselves**, so
140	  sensitive values never enter the log.
141	
142	When a DB is configured, the audit log also flows into `agent_job_events`
143	with `event_type = "tool_audit"`, joining the per-job event timeline used by
144	the M6 OTEL exporter.
145	
146	## Decision gate
147	
148	When a tool resolves to `ask`, the agent writes a decision record and pauses.
149	The CLI surface for humans is:
150	
151	```
152	Agent reached decision gate: Submit run kca-run-123 to Kaggle?
153	Operation: kaggle_submit
154	Skill: prepare-submission
155	Mode: competition-finalization
156	Audit: required
157	[approve] [deny] [explain]
158	```
159	
160	A human responds via `kca decision approve <id>` / `deny <id>`, which appends
161	an `approval_resume` event and unblocks `scripts/run_job.py --job-id <uuid>`.
162	
163	## Directory layout
164	
165	```
166	.kca/
````

1	"""Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, parse YAML frontmatter."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import re
6	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	import yaml
10	
11	
12	def _repo_root() -> Path:
13	    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
14	
15	
16	def _default_skills_root() -> Path:
17	    return _repo_root() / ".kca" / "skills"
18	
19	
20	@dataclass
21	class SkillMeta:
22	    name: str
23	    description: str
24	    version: str = "1.0"
25	    argument_hint: str = ""
26	    arguments: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
27	    allowed_tools: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
28	    approval_policy: str = "default"
29	    disable_model_invocation: bool = False
30	    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
31	    body: str = ""
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class Skill:
36	    meta: SkillMeta
37	    path: Path
38	    rendered_body: str = ""
39	
40	
41	_FRONTMATTER_RE = re.compile(
42	    r"\A---[ \t]*\r?\n(?P<fm>.*?)\r?\n---[ \t]*\r?\n?(?P<body>.*)\Z",
43	    re.DOTALL,
44	)
45	
46	
47	def _parse_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
48	    m = _FRONTMATTER_RE.match(text)
49	    if not m:
50	        return {}, text
51	    fm_text = m.group("fm")
52	    body = m.group("body")
53	    try:
54	        data = yaml.safe_load(fm_text) or {}
55	    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
56	        raise ValueError(f"malformed YAML frontmatter: {exc}") from exc
57	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
58	        raise ValueError("frontmatter must be a YAML mapping")
59	    return data, body
60	
61	
62	def _build_meta(data: dict, *, fallback_name: str) -> SkillMeta:
63	    name = data.get("name", fallback_name)
64	    description = data.get("description", "")
65	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
66	        raise ValueError("skill `name` is required and must be a string")
67	    if not isinstance(description, str):
68	        raise ValueError("skill `description` must be a string")
69	    version = str(data.get("version", "1.0"))
70	    argument_hint = str(data.get("argument-hint", data.get("argument_hint", "")))
71	    arguments = list(data.get("arguments", []) or [])
72	    allowed_tools = list(data.get("allowed-tools", data.get("allowed_tools", [])) or [])
73	    approval_policy = str(
74	        data.get("approval-policy", data.get("approval_policy", "default"))
75	    )
76	    disable_model_invocation = bool(
77	        data.get(
78	            "disable-model-invocation",
79	            data.get("disable_model_invocation", False),
80	        )
81	    )
82	    tags = list(data.get("tags", []) or [])
83	    return SkillMeta(
84	        name=name,
85	        description=description,
86	        version=version,
87	        argument_hint=argument_hint,
88	        arguments=[str(a) for a in arguments],
89	        allowed_tools=[str(t) for t in allowed_tools],
90	        approval_policy=approval_policy,
91	        disable_model_invocation=disable_model_invocation,
92	        tags=[str(t) for t in tags],
93	    )
94	
95	
96	def load_skill(name: str, *, skills_root: Path | None = None) -> Skill:
97	    root = skills_root or _default_skills_root()
98	    skill_dir = root / name
99	    skill_md = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"
100	    if not skill_md.is_file():
101	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"skill {name!r} not found at {skill_md}")
102	    text = skill_md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
103	    data, body = _parse_frontmatter(text)
104	    meta = _build_meta(data, fallback_name=name)
105	    meta.body = body
106	    return Skill(meta=meta, path=skill_md.resolve(), rendered_body=body)
107	
108	
109	def list_skills(*, skills_root: Path | None = None) -> list[SkillMeta]:
110	    root = skills_root or _default_skills_root()
111	    metas: list[SkillMeta] = []
112	    if not root.is_dir():
113	        return metas
114	    for entry in sorted(root.iterdir()):
115	        if not entry.is_dir():
116	            continue
117	        skill_md = entry / "SKILL.md"
118	        if not skill_md.is_file():
119	            continue
120	        try:
121	            skill = load_skill(entry.name, skills_root=root)
122	        except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError):
123	            continue
124	        metas.append(skill.meta)
125	    return metas
126	
127	
128	_ARG_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)")
129	
130	
131	def render_skill(skill: Skill, args: dict[str, str]) -> str:
132	    body = skill.meta.body
133	    # Verify declared arguments present.
134	    missing = [a for a in skill.meta.arguments if a not in args]
135	    if missing:
136	        raise ValueError(f"missing skill argument(s): {', '.join(missing)}")
137	
138	    def _sub(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
139	        key = match.group(1)
140	        if key in args:
141	            return str(args[key])
142	        return match.group(0)
143	
144	    rendered = _ARG_TOKEN_RE.sub(_sub, body)
145	    skill.rendered_body = rendered
146	    return rendered
147

```python
"""JSON-Schema-style validator for SKILL.md frontmatter.

We use a hand-rolled validator (no jsonschema dependency) keyed off
``SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA``. The shape and field names match the existing
M7 ``SkillMeta`` so we can fail loudly on unknown keys, malformed types, or
bad slugs without changing the loader contract.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["name", "description"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "properties": {
        "name": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-_]*$",
        },
        "description": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 280},
        "version": {"type": "string"},
        "argument-hint": {"type": "string"},
        "arguments": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "allowed-tools": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "approval-policy": {"type": "string"},
        "disable-model-invocation": {"type": "boolean"},
        "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    },
}


class SkillValidationError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a SKILL.md frontmatter does not match the schema."""


_TYPE_MAP: dict[str, tuple[type, ...]] = {
    "string": (str,),
    "boolean": (bool,),
    "array": (list,),
    "object": (dict,),
    "number": (int, float),
}


def _matches_type(value: Any, type_name: str) -> bool:
    expected = _TYPE_MAP.get(type_name)
    if expected is None:
        return True
    # booleans are ints in Python; exclude bool when expecting number/int.
    if type_name == "number" and isinstance(value, bool):
        return False
    return isinstance(value, expected)


def _validate_field(name: str, value: Any, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    type_name = spec.get("type")
    if type_name and not _matches_type(value, type_name):
        raise SkillValidationError(
            f"field {name!r}: expected type {type_name}, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )
    if type_name == "string":
        if "minLength" in spec and len(value) < spec["minLength"]:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: minLength {spec['minLength']} not met"
            )
        if "maxLength" in spec and len(value) > spec["maxLength"]:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: maxLength {spec['maxLength']} exceeded"
            )
        pattern = spec.get("pattern")
        if pattern and not re.match(pattern, value):
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: value {value!r} does not match pattern {pattern}"
            )
    if type_name == "array":
        item_spec = spec.get("items")
        if item_spec is None:
            return
        for i, item in enumerate(value):
            _validate_field(f"{name}[{i}]", item, item_spec)


def validate_frontmatter(data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Raise :class:`SkillValidationError` on schema mismatch."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise SkillValidationError("frontmatter must be a YAML mapping")
    schema = SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA

    for key in schema.get("required", []):
        if key not in data:
            raise SkillValidationError(f"required field missing: {key!r}")

    allowed = set(schema["properties"].keys())
    if not schema.get("additionalProperties", True):
        for key in data:
            if key not in allowed:
                raise SkillValidationError(f"unknown frontmatter key: {key!r}")

    for key, value in data.items():
        spec = schema["properties"].get(key)
        if spec is None:
            continue
        _validate_field(key, value, spec)


def validate_allowed_tools(allowed_tools: list[str], known_tools: set[str]) -> None:
    """Raise SkillValidationError when allowed_tools references unknown names."""
    for t in allowed_tools or []:
        if t not in known_tools:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"allowed-tools references unknown tool: {t!r} "
                f"(must be one of {sorted(known_tools)[:6]}…)"
            )

```

133	                max_side_effect=policy.max_side_effect,
134	            )
135	        # Allow test code to override the mock scenario or inject a client directly.
136	        self._mock_scenario: str = "two_turns"
137	        self._mock_client: MockLiteLLMClient | None = None
138	
139	    def run(self) -> WorkerResult:
140	        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel
141	
142	        # Only tag spans with a job_id when we know that row exists in the DB
143	        # (otherwise the Supabase exporter trips on the agent_jobs FK).
144	        tracer_job_id = self.job_id if self.db_url else None
145	        tracer = _otel.build_tracer(job_id=tracer_job_id)
146	        if tracer.is_enabled():
147	            job_span = _otel.start_job_span(tracer, self.job_id, self.prompt)
148	            try:
149	                if self.db_url and self.job_id:
150	                    self._safe_set_job_trace(tracer.trace_id, job_span.span_id)
151	            except Exception:
152	                pass
153	        else:
154	            job_span = None
155	        try:
156	            return self._run_inner(tracer)
157	        finally:
158	            if job_span is not None:
159	                job_span.end()

161	    def _safe_set_job_trace(self, trace_id: str, root_span_id: str) -> None:
162	        try:
163	            import sys as _sys
164	
165	            _sys.path.insert(
166	                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
167	            )
168	            import db as _db
169	
170	            _db.set_job_trace(self.job_id, trace_id, root_span_id)
171	        except Exception:
172	            pass

174	    def _run_inner(self, tracer) -> WorkerResult:
175	        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel
176	
177	        if self._mock_client is not None:
178	            client = self._mock_client
179	        elif self.dry_run:
180	            client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario=self._mock_scenario)
181	        else:
182	            client = None
183	        budget = BudgetTracker(self.policy, model=self.policy.model)
184	        # Seed from resume_state so cumulative turns/cost roll forward.
185	        if self.resume_state:
186	            budget.turns = int(self.resume_state.get("turns_used") or 0)
187	            budget.cost_usd = float(self.resume_state.get("cost_usd") or 0.0)
188	        executor = ToolExecutor(self.workspace, self.policy)
189	        # One-shot allowlist for the paused tool_input from a prior pause.
190	        allow_once = (self.resume_state or {}).get("allow_once") or None
191	        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": self.prompt}]
192	        start = time.monotonic()
193	
194	        while True:
195	            # 1. Pre-turn budget check
196	            stop_reason = budget.check_limits()
197	            if stop_reason:
198	                self._update_status("failed", error=stop_reason, budget=budget)
199	                return WorkerResult(
200	                    status="budget_stop",
201	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
202	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
203	                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
204	                    final_message="",
205	                    stop_reason=stop_reason,
206	                )
207	
208	            # 2. LiteLLM call (OpenAI format for all providers)
209	            extra: dict = (
210	                {} if self.policy.min_p is None else {"min_p": self.policy.min_p}
211	            )
212	            with _otel.with_turn_span(tracer, budget.turns + 1) as _turn_span:
213	                if client is not None:
214	                    response = client.completion(
215	                        model=self.policy.model,
216	                        max_tokens=8192,
217	                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
218	                        messages=messages,
219	                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
220	                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
221	                        **extra,
222	                    )
223	                else:
224	                    import litellm
225	
226	                    response = litellm.completion(
227	                        model=self.policy.model,
228	                        max_tokens=8192,
229	                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
230	                        messages=messages,
231	                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
232	                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
233	                        **extra,
234	                    )
235	                if _turn_span is not None:
236	                    _turn_span.set_attribute("model", self.policy.model)
237	                    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
238	                    if usage is not None:
239	                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
240	                            "prompt_tokens",
241	                            getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
242	                        )
243	                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
244	                            "completion_tokens",
245	                            getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
246	                        )
247	
248	            # 3. Record turn cost
249	            budget.record_turn(response)
250	            msg = response.choices[0].message
251	            finish_reason = response.choices[0].finish_reason
252	
253	            self._append_event(
254	                "turn_start",
255	                budget.turns,
256	                input_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
257	                output_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
258	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
259	                event_data={"finish_reason": finish_reason},
260	            )
261	
262	            # 4. stop → job done
263	            if finish_reason == "stop":
264	                final_text = msg.content or ""
265	                self._update_status("succeeded", budget=budget)
266	                return WorkerResult(
267	                    status="done",
268	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
269	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
270	                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
271	                    final_message=final_text,
272	                    stop_reason="end_turn",
273	                )
274	
275	            # 5. tool_calls → execute each tool
276	            if finish_reason == "tool_calls":
277	                tool_calls = msg.tool_calls or []
278	                # Append assistant turn with tool_calls (OpenAI message format)
279	                messages.append(
280	                    {
281	                        "role": "assistant",
282	                        "content": msg.content,
283	                        "tool_calls": [
284	                            {
285	                                "id": tc.id,
286	                                "type": "function",
287	                                "function": {
288	                                    "name": tc.function.name,
289	                                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
290	                                },
291	                            }
292	                            for tc in tool_calls
293	                        ],
294	                    }
295	                )
296	                for tc in tool_calls:
297	                    tool_input = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
298	                    self._append_event(
299	                        "tool_call",
300	                        budget.turns,
301	                        event_data={"tool": tc.function.name, "input": tool_input},
302	                    )
303	                    try:
304	                        with _otel.with_tool_span(tracer, tc.function.name, tool_input):
305	                            result_content = executor.execute(
306	                                tc.function.name, tool_input
307	                            )
308	                    except ApprovalRequired as exc:
309	                        # One-shot resume allowance: bypass the matching gate
310	                        # exactly once after `kca decisions approve`.
311	                        if allow_once and (
312	                            allow_once.get("operation") == exc.tool_name
313	                            or allow_once.get("operation") == "tool_approval"
314	                        ):
315	                            allow_once = None  # consume
316	                            # Recurse into the actual tool with policy bypass
317	                            # by temporarily relaxing max_side_effect for this
318	                            # one call.
319	                            saved = executor.policy.max_side_effect
320	                            executor.policy.max_side_effect = "SUBMISSION"
321	                            try:
322	                                result_content = executor.execute(
323	                                    tc.function.name, tool_input
324	                                )
325	                            finally:
326	                                executor.policy.max_side_effect = saved
327	                        else:
328	                            return self._handle_approval_required(exc, budget, start)
329	
330	                    self._append_event(
331	                        "tool_result",
332	                        budget.turns,
333	                        event_data={
334	                            "tool": tc.function.name,
335	                            "result_preview": str(result_content)[:200],
336	                        },
337	                    )
338	                    messages.append(
339	                        {
340	                            "role": "tool",
341	                            "tool_call_id": tc.id,
342	                            "content": str(result_content),
343	                        }
344	                    )
345	                continue
346	
347	            # 6. Unexpected finish_reason
348	            self._update_status(
349	                "failed",
350	                error=f"unexpected finish_reason={finish_reason}",
351	                budget=budget,
352	            )
353	            return WorkerResult(
354	                status="failed",
355	                turns_used=budget.turns,
356	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
357	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
358	                final_message="",
359	                stop_reason="unexpected",
360	            )
361	
362	    def _handle_approval_required(
363	        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker, start: float
364	    ) -> WorkerResult:
365	        """Pause the job and record a decision request.
366	
367	        M6: when the gating operation is one of KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS,
368	        first consult the sync reviewer. Reviewer.approve auto-resumes,
369	        reviewer.reject either escalates to humans (default) or fails the
370	        job (when KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT=0), and reviewer.abstain
371	        falls through to the existing human-decisions path.
372	        """
373	        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
374	        # M6 reviewer pre-check
375	        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
376	        reviewer_outcome = self._maybe_consult_reviewer(exc, budget)
377	        if reviewer_outcome == "approve":
378	            # Re-execute the gated tool with one-shot bypass.
379	            return WorkerResult(
380	                status="reviewer_approved",
381	                turns_used=budget.turns,
382	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
383	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
384	                final_message="reviewer approved",
385	                stop_reason="reviewer_approve",
386	            )
387	        if reviewer_outcome == "reject_fail":
388	            self._update_status(
389	                "failed",
390	                error="reviewer rejected high-stakes operation",
391	                budget=budget,
392	            )
393	            return WorkerResult(
394	                status="failed",
395	                turns_used=budget.turns,
396	                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
397	                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
398	                final_message="",
399	                stop_reason="reviewer_reject",
400	            )
401	        # reviewer_outcome in {None, "reject_escalate", "abstain"} — fall
402	        # through to human-decisions flow.
403	        decision_id = None
404	        if self.db_url:
405	            try:
406	                import sys
407	
408	                sys.path.insert(
409	                    0,
410	                    str(
411	                        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"
412	                    ),
413	                )
414	                import db as _db
415	
416	                decision_id = _db.insert_approval_request(
417	                    decision_type="tool_approval",
418	                    prompt=f"Worker job {self.job_id} wants to call {exc.tool_name}",
419	                    options={
420	                        "approve": "allow this tool call",
421	                        "deny": "block and stop job",
422	                    },
423	                    job_id=self.job_id,
424	                )
425	                _db.update_job(
426	                    self.job_id,
427	                    status="paused",
428	                    turns_used=budget.turns,
429	                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
430	                )
431	            except Exception:
432	                pass
433	        self._append_event(
434	            "approval_pause",
435	            budget.turns,
436	            event_data={
437	                "tool": exc.tool_name,
438	                "operation": exc.tool_name,
439	                "tool_input": exc.tool_input,
440	                "side_effect": exc.side_effect,
441	                "decision_id": decision_id,
442	            },
443	        )
444	        import sys
445	
446	        print(
447	            f"JOB PAUSED — run `kca decisions approve --id {decision_id}` to resume",
448	            file=sys.stderr,
449	        )
450	        return WorkerResult(
451	            status="paused",
452	            turns_used=budget.turns,
453	            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
454	            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
455	            final_message=f"Waiting for approval: decision_id={decision_id}",
456	            stop_reason="approval_required",
457	        )

459	    @classmethod
460	    def resume(
461	        cls,
462	        job_id: str,
463	        *,
464	        workspace: Path,
465	        policy: JobPolicy | None = None,
466	        db_url: str | None = None,
467	        dry_run: bool = False,
468	    ) -> "AgentWorker":
469	        """Construct an AgentWorker primed from prior agent_job_events.
470	
471	        Reads the job row + events; reconstructs (turns_used, cost_usd) and
472	        seeds a one-shot approval allowlist for the paused tool_input so the
473	        next gate check passes once.
474	        """
475	        import sys as _sys
476	
477	        _sys.path.insert(
478	            0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
479	        )
480	        import db as _db
481	
482	        job = _db.get_job(job_id)
483	        events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
484	        turns = int(job.get("turns_used") or 0)
485	        cost = float(job.get("cost_usd") or 0)
486	        last_pause_input = None
487	        last_pause_op = None
488	        # Walk events: the most recent approval_pause defines the next-resume
489	        # allowlist entry, unless followed by an approval_resume already
490	        # consumed in a previous resume attempt.
491	        for ev in events:
492	            t = ev.get("event_type")
493	            ed = ev.get("event_data") or {}
494	            if isinstance(ed, str):
495	                try:
496	                    ed = json.loads(ed)
497	                except Exception:
498	                    ed = {}
499	            if t == "approval_pause":
500	                last_pause_input = ed.get("tool_input")
501	                last_pause_op = ed.get("operation") or ed.get("tool")
502	            elif t == "approval_resume":
503	                # Resume consumed; clear pending allowance.
504	                last_pause_input = None
505	                last_pause_op = None
506	        prompt = job.get("prompt") or ""
507	        policy = policy or JobPolicy()
508	        worker = cls(
509	            job_id=job_id,
510	            prompt=prompt,
511	            policy=policy,
512	            workspace=workspace,
513	            db_url=db_url,
514	            dry_run=dry_run,
515	            resume_state={
516	                "turns_used": turns,
517	                "cost_usd": cost,
518	                "allow_once": {
519	                    "operation": last_pause_op,
520	                    "tool_input": last_pause_input,
521	                }
522	                if last_pause_op
523	                else None,
524	            },
525	        )
526	        return worker
527	
528	    def _maybe_consult_reviewer(
529	        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker
530	    ) -> str | None:
531	        """Run the sync reviewer for trigger ops; return outcome tag.
532	
533	        Returns one of:
534	          None             — reviewer not consulted (op not in trigger set or
535	                              already reviewed)
536	          "approve"        — reviewer approved; caller resumes the tool
537	          "reject_fail"    — reviewer rejected and ESCALATE_REJECT=0
538	          "reject_escalate"— reviewer rejected, caller should page humans
539	          "abstain"        — reviewer abstained, caller should page humans
540	        """
541	        from src.worker.reviewer import (
542	            Reviewer,
543	            ReviewRequest,
544	            should_consult_reviewer,
545	            escalate_reject,
546	        )
547	
548	        target_op = exc.tool_name
549	        if not should_consult_reviewer(target_op):
550	            return None
551	        if not self.db_url:
552	            # No DB → no event trail and no place to record the verdict.
553	            # The dry-run worker still records the reviewer span via OTEL when
554	            # T005 wires it up; for now just skip silently.
555	            return None
556	        try:
557	            import sys as _sys
558	
559	            _sys.path.insert(
560	                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
561	            )
562	            import db as _db
563	
564	            # Skip if reviewer already ran for (job_id, target_op).
565	            try:
566	                existing = _db.find_review_for_op(self.job_id, target_op)
567	            except Exception:
568	                existing = None
569	            if existing is not None:
570	                return None
571	            events = []
572	            try:
573	                events = _db.list_job_events(self.job_id)
574	            except Exception:
575	                events = []
576	            req = ReviewRequest(
577	                job_id=self.job_id,
578	                target_op=target_op,
579	                tool_name=exc.tool_name,
580	                tool_input=exc.tool_input,
581	                final_message=None,
582	                event_trail=events,
583	            )
584	            reviewer = Reviewer(dry_run=self.dry_run)
585	            verdict = reviewer.review(req)
586	            try:
587	                _db.create_review(
588	                    job_id=self.job_id,
589	                    reviewer_model=verdict.reviewer_model,
590	                    verdict=verdict.verdict,
591	                    target_op=target_op,
592	                    rationale=verdict.rationale,
593	                    evidence=verdict.evidence,
594	                    cost_usd=verdict.cost_usd,
595	                )
596	            except Exception:
597	                pass
598	            if verdict.verdict == "approve":
599	                self._append_event(
600	                    "approval_resume",
601	                    budget.turns,
602	                    event_data={
603	                        "source": "reviewer",
604	                        "verdict": "approve",
605	                        "target_op": target_op,
606	                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
607	                    },
608	                )
609	                return "approve"
610	            if verdict.verdict == "reject":
611	                if escalate_reject():
612	                    self._append_event(
613	                        "reviewer_reject",
614	                        budget.turns,
615	                        event_data={
616	                            "target_op": target_op,
617	                            "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
618	                            "escalated": True,
619	                        },
620	                    )
621	                    return "reject_escalate"
622	                self._append_event(
623	                    "reviewer_reject",
624	                    budget.turns,
625	                    event_data={
626	                        "target_op": target_op,
627	                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
628	                        "escalated": False,
629	                    },
630	                )
631	                return "reject_fail"
632	            # abstain → fall through
633	            self._append_event(
634	                "reviewer_abstain",
635	                budget.turns,
636	                event_data={
637	                    "target_op": target_op,
638	                    "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
639	                },
640	            )
641	            return "abstain"
642	        except Exception:
643	            return None
644
